name: Zhu Jing Wan
summary: A classical three-herb pill that strengthens the Liver and Kidneys, nourishes the blood and essence, and sharpens eyesight. It is traditionally used for declining vision, blurry sight, floaters, and dark shadows in front of the eyes caused by deficiency of the Liver and Kidneys.
tcm_actions: ["Tonifies the Liver and Kidneys", "Nourishes Jing and Blood", "Brightens the eyes and improves vision"]
therapeutic_focus: ["Eye health", "Vision support", "Aging gracefully", "Tonic for Liver and Kidney"]
dynasty: Tai Ping Sheng Hui Fang (太平圣惠方), Volume 33
conditions: ["Age-Related Macular Degeneration", "Diabetic Retinopathy", "Floaters (Vitreous Degeneration)", "Cataracts (Early Stage)", "Central Serous Chorioretinopathy", "Retinitis Pigmentosa", "Optic Nerve Atrophy", "Dry Eye Syndrome", "Visual Fatigue (Asthenopia)", "Myopia (Progressive)"]
pregnancy: Contraindicated during pregnancy. Although Tu Si Zi (Cuscuta) is sometimes used in small, carefully monitored doses for threatened miscarriage in other formulas, the overall composition and dosage of this formula are considered unsafe during pregnancy. Avoid use unless under strict professional supervision where deemed absolutely necessary.
breastfeeding: No specific data on breast milk transfer exists for the herbs in this formula. Caution is advised during breastfeeding. Use only under professional guidance; some components may affect milk composition or the nursing infant.
children: Not typically prescribed for children. If used in adolescents for myopia or other conditions, dosage must be significantly reduced and treatment overseen by a pediatric TCM specialist. The formula is primarily designed for age-related visual decline and may not be appropriate for most pediatric eye conditions.
drug_interactions: No well-documented drug interactions. Consult a healthcare provider before concurrent use with prescription medications.
best_time_to_take: Take on an empty stomach (at least 30 minutes before meals), once in the morning and once before the evening meal. Traditionally taken with warm rice wine or lightly salted water to guide the herbs to the Kidneys.
typical_duration: Typically prescribed for 8–12 weeks, with reassessment after 4 weeks. Long-term use should be monitored for any digestive side effects.
dietary_advice: Avoid cold, raw, and difficult-to-digest foods while taking this tonic formula to protect Spleen function and prevent dampness. Limit greasy, fried, and spicy foods. The classical preparation uses warm wine or salt water as a vehicle; however, heavy alcohol consumption beyond the medicinal use should be avoided.

ingredients.role_description: Tonifies both the yin and the yang of the Liver and Kidneys, directly brightens the eyes, and anchors the essence. Its balanced, gentle nature makes it the central ingredient for treating visual weakness due to deficiency.
Richly nourishes Kidney yin and blood, fills the essence, and strengthens the foundation of the Liver and Kidneys, so that the eyes are properly moistened and nourished.

research.title: A randomized controlled trial of modified Zhujing Pills for dry age-related macular degeneration (2024)
research.description: In a 64-patient RCT (32 per arm), patients with dry age-related macular degeneration of the Liver-Kidney insufficiency type received either modified Zhujing Pills granules or a control treatment for 3 months. The Zhujing Pill group showed significantly improved visual acuity, reduced drusen area, decreased fundus autofluorescence intensity, and increased plasma SOD and GSH-Px activities, with reduced MDA levels. The therapeutic mechanism may involve activation of the Nrf2/Keap1 antioxidant pathway.
research.periodical: Feng SQ, Zhou X, Zhang YZ, et al. Clinical Study on the Treatment of Dry Age-Related Macular Degeneration of Liver and Kidney Insufficiency Type with Modified Zhujing Pills. J Nanjing Univ Tradit Chin Med. 2024;40(5):521-526.
